name: Soul Shatter
oracle_text: Each opponent sacrifices a creature or planeswalker with the greatest mana value among creatures and planeswalkers they control.
blocked_sentences: Each opponent sacrifices a creature or planeswalker with the greatest mana value among creatures and planeswalkers they control.

needs.what: a control op that runs a body once per player from a `players` spec (`each_opponent`, `each_player`), binding the current player so nested effects and their selectors resolve against that one player -- so that `sacrifice`, `destroy` and friends can happen once per opponent instead of once in total
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `for_each` iterates *objects* and binds `each` to an oid; there is no player-shaped loop. The `player` spec (`select_players`) exists but only ops that act on a player directly -- `discard`, `mill`, `shuffle`, `draw`, `lose_life` -- read it; `sacrifice` takes only an `objects` selector, so a single sacrifice op over `{"controller": "opponent", "count": 1}` removes one permanent across the union of all opponents' boards, not one from each. `count: "all"` overshoots and takes every matching permanent from every opponent.

needs.what: a way for a selector's `controller` clause to name a player bound by the enclosing loop (e.g. `"controller": {"player": "each"}`), so that `extreme` and `chooser` are evaluated within that one player's permanents
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `controller` accepts only `"you"`, `"opponent"` (meaning every opponent at once) or anything else (all players), so the pool for "among creatures and planeswalkers they control" cannot be scoped to a single opponent. `extreme` then computes one global maximum over the merged pool -- in a 3-player game the opponent with the smaller top mana value would be spared entirely -- and `chooser: "owner"` asks only the owner of `pool[0]`, so one opponent would be choosing another opponent's sacrifice.
